description.short_caption: Lateral chest radiograph showing thoracic structures.
description.detailed_description: This is a lateral chest radiograph displaying the thoracic cavity. The image shows the vertebral column, ribs, and soft tissue structures. The diaphragm is visible inferiorly, and the lung fields appear partially aerated. No obvious consolidation, pleural effusion, or gross abnormalities are apparent in this image. The radiograph is well-positioned, with clear visualization of the thoracic spine and posterior ribs.

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing bilateral lung fields and mediastinal structures.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph displaying both lung fields, the mediastinum, and the diaphragm. The lung fields appear clear without obvious consolidations, masses, or effusions. The heart silhouette is visible, and the mediastinum appears midline. The bony structures, including the ribs and clavicles, are intact. No significant abnormalities are immediately apparent in this image.
